doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Rock concerts in San Francisco and a firehouse rehearsal
summary: Too young for clubs, he heard Cream, Hendrix, Monterey Pop and Altamont, and listened to Big Brother and the Holding Company rehearse.

bands.name: Big Brother and the Holding Company
Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Can you describe specifically what a night, taking a bus to hear some music was like for you? Were they nightclubs?

So I’m too young to go to nightclubs, okay? It’s, I think the most perverse thing about my life and career is that I wasn’t 21 until 1971, which means I couldn’t possibly have heard all this great stuff live. I was just there — you know turned 21, Art Blakey and the Messengers at the Keystone Korner in San Francisco with Bobby Watson. You know that’s where I kind of jump into hearing it live. And so what we’re talking about is a fantastic, unbelievable upbringing in rock music in San Francisco. From the age of 14 I went to everything. I heard the debut of Cream and Hendrix at The Fillmore. I went to the Monterey Pop Festival, to Altamont, as crappy as it was. I heard The Who four times you know. Hendrix doing a cover of Sgt. Pepper’s at Winterland. It was all rock music and trying to play jazz on the saxophone but listening to rock music ‘cause that’s what I could go to hear live. And that was stuff that was originally at Longshoreman’s Hall in the Marina in San Francisco in the time before The Fillmore got started. So you know, taking a bus down there. After that, the Avalon Ballroom and The Fillmore and then The Fillmore in another location downtown on Market Street. The Fillmore was in the Fillmore District, which is one of the African-American districts in San Francisco, and then it moved downtown to Market Street to a much more generic location. So yeah, I could go on and on. All right I’ll tell you the most incredible thing. So there was a firehouse, a disused firehouse 2-1/2 blocks from our home. And I had a friend who was cutting edge everything you know. He was the first person with a skateboard, with a surfboard, unfortunately with drugs and really ruined his life. And he was just on top of everything with music. He would be the one who said, “Hey, this group called Cream is

Coming to The Fillmore.” And so he took me around to this firehouse where this band was rehearsing with Sears Danelectro amplifiers. And it was Big Brother and the Holding Company before Janis Joplin joined them. And so we would go up there and just listen to them doing these two-chord jams you know, two guitar jams, sorry, not two-chord jams.

No, no, no, not necessarily. They were, I actually liked them a lot more without Janis. They were great improvisers and had really interesting two-line things going. So you know that was the kind of thing that I was able to hear.
